scout.purpose: Reactive features combine changing sources and replace, concatenate, or concurrently merge inner streams according to product ordering semantics.
scout.realWorldUse: Search queries, filters, account changes, database joins, dependent data, and concurrent event processing rely on the correct combining operator.
scout.outcome: Choose combine, zip, flatMapLatest, flatMapConcat, or flatMapMerge and explain cancellation and ordering.

sections.title: combine and zip answer different timing questions

blocks.text: combine emits after each source has a value and then whenever either changes, using the latest value from each. It suits query plus filters or local entities plus user preference. zip pairs the first with first, second with second, and completes according to paired availability; it fits positional correspondence rather than UI state. combine with many sources can produce broad recomputation, so derive focused models and test startup when one source has not emitted.

blocks.caption: Each latest request replaces obsolete search collection after the debounce boundary.

blocks.text: flatMapConcat collects each inner Flow fully in order. flatMapMerge collects multiple inner flows concurrently with bounded concurrency and interleaves their outputs. flatMapLatest cancels the previous inner collection when a new outer value arrives, fitting search or selected-account replacement. Cancellation must reach the underlying source for obsolete work to stop. mapLatest transforms one value with replacement without requiring an inner Flow.

blocks.caption: Each latest request replaces obsolete search collection after the debounce boundary.

blocks.title: Choose from product ordering
blocks.text: Latest, ordered, paired, and concurrent are different user-visible contracts.

sections.title: Latest replacement is cancellation, not magic deduplication

blocks.text: Use debounce and distinctUntilChanged before expensive search replacement when product behaviour permits. StateFlow already suppresses equal values using equality, so redundant distinct operations may have no effect. Do not use flatMapLatest for writes that must complete; replacement cancellation could abandon user intent. When every event matters, process a queue or use concat semantics. Test rapid inputs with a fake source that records start, cancellation, completion, and output identity.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.text: A new event can abandon a prior operation that must complete.

inspect.title: Replace zip in UI state
walkthrough: zip waits for matching emission positions from both sources.
Changing the query repeatedly may wait for equally many filter emissions.
combine should recalculate with the latest filter whenever either source changes.
inspect.expectedOutput: Every accepted query or filter change produces a request from the latest pair.

trap_check.mistake: Using flatMapLatest for queued bookmark writes.
trap_check.why: A second bookmark event cancels the first before durable completion.
trap_check.fix: Use sequential processing or explicitly durable work semantics.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Combine query and filters, debounce input, replace obsolete searches, and test rapid changes, cancellation, initial state, and errors.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Latest accepted request owns visible results. Old source collection is demonstrably cancelled. Durable selection events use a non-cancelling path.

recall.answer: The latest value from every source.

recall.prompt: What does flatMapLatest do to old inner Flow?
recall.answer: Cancels it when a new outer value arrives.
